partI_summary.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community engagement, and shared access to tools and facilities for members of all skill levels.

partIII_programServiceAccomplishments.missionStatement: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild promotes the art and craft of woodworking through education, community engagement, and shared access to tools and facilities for members of all skill levels.

programServices.description: Membership program providing woodworking enthusiasts access to guild facilities, tools, educational workshops, special interest groups (SIGs), and monthly meetings. Membership dues collected during the tax year totaled $250.00 (one payment on record for 2025; see Schedule O data quality note regarding possible test transaction). The guild offers classes including Rough to Ready, Basic Woodworking, Intermediate Woodworking, Bandsaw Box, Project Finishing, and Intro to Hand Tool Woodworking, as well as ongoing SIGs in CNC, Carving, Finishing, Hand Tools, and Laser Engraving.

Educational classes and workshops in woodworking techniques open to members and the public. Events include structured courses taught by volunteer instructors covering foundational and advanced woodworking skills. No event registration revenue was recorded within the 2025 tax year from verified non-test transactions.

Community outreach and public engagement activities including participation in the National Craft Open Studios Weekend, providing public demonstrations of woodworking craft and promoting awareness of the guild's educational mission.

partI_publicCharityStatus.description: Organization described in section 509(a)(2) — receives more than one-third of its support from contributions, membership fees, and gross receipts from activities related to its exempt functions, and not more than one-third from gross investment income and unrelated business taxable income. As a membership-based woodworking guild providing educational programs and community access to facilities, the organization qualifies under section 509(a)(2).

scheduleO.narrative: The Kansas City Woodworkers Guild Inc. is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit corporation founded in 1992 and based in Kansas City, Missouri. The organization's mission is to promote the art and craft of woodworking through education, community engagement, and shared access to tools and facilities. The guild serves members of all skill levels through monthly meetings, structured woodworking classes (including Rough to Ready, Basic Woodworking, Intermediate Woodworking, Bandsaw Box, Project Finishing, and Intro to Hand Tool Woodworking), special interest groups (CNC, Carving, Finishing, Hand Tools, and Laser Engraving), and public outreach events such as the National Craft Open Studios Weekend.

The Form 990 was prepared by the organization's Treasurer, John A Steyer, using QuickBooks and WildApricot financial data. The completed return was not formally distributed to all governing body members prior to filing due to the organization's small volunteer-run structure. The Treasurer reviews the return before submission. The organization intends to implement a formal governing body review process in future years.

The organization makes its governing documents, conflict of interest policy (if adopted), and financial statements available to the public upon written request directed to the Treasurer at 1717 Washington St, Kansas City, MO 64108-1121. The organization does not currently post these documents on a public website.

scheduleO.partAndLine: Part XI Line 8 — Prior Period Adjustment
scheduleO.narrative: Part XI, Line 8 reflects a prior period adjustment of $4,740.00 representing the QuickBooks Opening Balance Equity of $5,000.00 less current year revenue in excess of expenses of $260.00. The QuickBooks equity section contains only an Opening Balance Equity entry of $5,000.00 with null Retained Earnings and null Net Income, indicating the accounting system was newly configured during or prior to the 2025 tax year. No prior-year Form 990 ending net asset balance was available to populate the beginning-of-year column. The $5,000.00 in the Checking account is believed to represent initial organizational funding or a capital contribution not recorded through the income statement. The preparer should confirm the nature of this entry and reconcile to any prior-year Form 990 before filing. If prior-year ending net assets were greater than zero, Line 4 should be updated accordingly and Line 8 adjusted.

This amount has been included in 2025 contributions based on the absence of a date indicating it falls outside the tax year. The preparer should confirm the date of this donation before filing.

scheduleO.partAndLine: Part VIII Line 2a — Data Quality Note: Membership Payment
scheduleO.narrative: One WildApricot payment of $250.00 (Payment ID 106800163, dated 2025-08-05) was recorded under the name 'Testing, Scott' as a MembershipApplication invoice payment. This is the only WildApricot transaction dated within the 2025 tax year. The record bears characteristics of a test transaction (name includes 'Testing'). The preparer should verify whether this represents a bona fide membership payment or a system test entry. If confirmed as a test record, this $250.00 should be excluded from revenue and total revenue revised to $10.00. All other WildApricot invoices and payments are dated April through June 2026 and are outside the 2025 tax year.

scheduleO.partAndLine: Part X — Data Quality Flags Summary
scheduleO.narrative: The following data quality issues affect the 2025 balance sheet and should be resolved before filing: (1) QuickBooks Profit and Loss report returned all null values for the 2025 tax year — no expense line items are available; (2) QuickBooks Balance Sheet shows no liability accounts — all liability lines are set to $0.00; (3) QuickBooks equity consists entirely of Opening Balance Equity of $5,000.00 with null Retained Earnings and null Net Income, suggesting incomplete QuickBooks setup; (4) No prior-year (2024-12-31) balance sheet data was provided — all beginning-of-year amounts are set to $0.00 and must be populated from the prior year Form 990 Part X before filing; (5) All WildApricot invoice and payment records except one are dated April through June 2026 and fall outside the 2025 tax year; (6) WildApricot contains apparent test records that have been excluded from financial reporting. The preparer must address all flagged items prior to submission.

Prior year support data (2021–2024) is not available from the source systems provided. The five-year support schedule for Schedule A Part III reflects only the 2025 tax year amount of $260.00 (contributions, gifts, grants, and membership fees). The public support percentage and investment income percentage cannot be calculated without prior-year data. The organization's status as a publicly supported organization under section 509(a)(2) is classified as Undetermined pending completion of the full five-year support schedule. The preparer should obtain prior-year Form 990 data to complete the support schedule before filing.
